sections.title: class Countdown
sections.body:
Custom iterator that counts down from a number.

```python
class Countdown:
    """Custom iterator that counts down from a number."""

    def __init__(self, start):
        self.current = start

    def __iter__(self):
        """Return the iterator object (self)."""
        return self

    def __next__(self):
        """Return the next item in the sequence."""
        if self.current <= 0:
            raise StopIteration

        self.current -= 1
        return self.current + 1

# Using the custom iterator
countdown = Countdown(5)
print("Counting down from 5:")
for num in countdown:
    print(num, end=" ")
print("\n")

# Manual iteration
countdown2 = Countdown(3)
iterator = iter(countdown2)
print("Manual iteration:")
try:
    print(next(iterator))  # 3
    print(next(iterator))  # 2
    print(next(iterator))  # 1
    print(next(iterator))  # Raises StopIteration
except StopIteration:
    print("Iterator exhausted")
print()
```

sections.title: simple_generator(), fibonacci()
sections.body:
Generate numbers from 0 to n-1. Generate first n Fibonacci numbers.

    Args:
        n: Number of Fibonacci numbers to generate

    Yields:
        int: Next Fibonacci number

```python
def simple_generator(n):
    """Generate numbers from 0 to n-1."""
    print(f"Generator started with n={n}")
    for i in range(n):
        print(f"About to yield {i}")
        yield i
        print(f"Resumed after yielding {i}")

print("Creating generator:")
gen = simple_generator(3)
print(f"Generator object: {gen}")
print(f"Type: {type(gen)}\n")

print("Iterating through generator:")
for value in gen:
    print(f"Received: {value}\n")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 3: Fibonacci Generator
# ============================================================================
print("=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 3: Fibonacci Generator")
print("=" * 70)

def fibonacci(n):
    """
    Generate first n Fibonacci numbers.

    Args:
        n: Number of Fibonacci numbers to generate

    Yields:
        int: Next Fibonacci number
    """
    a, b = 0, 1
    count = 0

    while count < n:
        yield a
        a, b = b, a + b
        count += 1

print("First 10 Fibonacci numbers:")
fib_gen = fibonacci(10)
for num in fib_gen:
    print(num, end=" ")
print("\n")

# Using generator in list comprehension
fib_list = list(fibonacci(15))
print(f"First 15 Fibonacci numbers: {fib_list}")
print()
```

sections.title: infinite_counter()
sections.body:
Generate an infinite sequence of numbers.

    Args:
        start: Starting number
        step: Increment value

    Yields:
        int/float: Next number in sequence

```python
def infinite_counter(start=0, step=1):
    """
    Generate an infinite sequence of numbers.

    Args:
        start: Starting number
        step: Increment value

    Yields:
        int/float: Next number in sequence
    """
    current = start
    while True:
        yield current
        current += step

# Use with caution - can run forever!
print("First 10 numbers from infinite counter:")
counter = infinite_counter(start=1, step=2)
for i, num in enumerate(counter):
    if i >= 10:
        break
    print(num, end=" ")
print("\n")
```

sections.title: running_average(), read_data(), filter_even() …
sections.body:
Calculate running average of sent values.

    Yields:
        float: Current running average Read data from source. Filter even numbers. Square each number.

```python
def running_average():
    """
    Calculate running average of sent values.

    Yields:
        float: Current running average
    """
    total = 0
    count = 0
    average = None

    while True:
        # Receive value sent to generator
        value = yield average
        if value is None:
            break
        total += value
        count += 1
        average = total / count

# Using send() to send values into generator
avg_gen = running_average()
next(avg_gen)  # Prime the generator

print("Calculating running average:")
print(f"Send 10: {avg_gen.send(10)}")
print(f"Send 20: {avg_gen.send(20)}")
print(f"Send 30: {avg_gen.send(30)}")
print(f"Send 40: {avg_gen.send(40)}")
print()

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 7: Generator Pipeline for Data Processing
# ============================================================================
print("=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 7: Generator Pipeline for Data Processing")
print("=" * 70)

def read_data(data):
    """Read data from source."""
    print("Reading data...")
    for item in data:
        yield item

def filter_even(numbers):
    """Filter even numbers."""
    print("Filtering even numbers...")
    for num in numbers:
        if num % 2 == 0:
            yield num

def square_numbers(numbers):
    """Square each number."""
    print("Squaring numbers...")
    for num in numbers:
        yield num**2
```

```python
def add_ten(numbers):
    """Add 10 to each number."""
    print("Adding 10 to numbers...")
    for num in numbers:
        yield num + 10

# Create pipeline
source_data = range(1, 11)
pipeline = add_ten(square_numbers(filter_even(read_data(source_data))))

print("Processing pipeline:")

print(f"Results: {results}\n")

def generator1():
    """First generator."""
    for i in range(1, 4):
        yield i

def generator2():
    """Second generator."""
    for i in range(4, 7):
        yield i

def combined_generator():
    """Combine multiple generators using yield from."""
    yield from generator1()
    yield from generator2()
    yield from [7, 8, 9]  # Can also delegate to any iterable

print("Combined generator output:")
for value in combined_generator():
    print(value, end=" ")
print("\n")
```

sections.title: flatten()
sections.body:
Flatten a nested list recursively.

    Args:
        nested_list: List that may contain nested lists

    Yields:
        Elements from the flattened list

```python
# Practical example: Flattening nested structures
def flatten(nested_list):
    """
    Flatten a nested list recursively.

    Args:
        nested_list: List that may contain nested lists

    Yields:
        Elements from the flattened list
    """
    for item in nested_list:
        if isinstance(item, list):
            yield from flatten(item)  # Recursive delegation
        else:
            yield item

nested = [1, [2, 3, [4, 5]], 6, [7, [8, 9]]]
print(f"Nested list: {nested}")
print(f"Flattened: {list(flatten(nested))}")
print()
```

sections.title: read_file_generator()
sections.body:
Read file line by line using generator.
    Memory efficient for large files.

    Args:
        filename: Path to file

    Yields:
        str: Each line from the file

```python
def read_file_generator(filename):
    """
    Read file line by line using generator.
    Memory efficient for large files.

    Args:
        filename: Path to file

    Yields:
        str: Each line from the file
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            for line in file:
                yield line.strip()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"File {filename} not found")
        return

# Create sample file
sample_file = "sample_data.txt"
with open(sample_file, "w") as f:
    f.write("Line 1: Hello\n")
    f.write("Line 2: World\n")
    f.write("Line 3: Python\n")
    f.write("Line 4: Generators\n")
    f.write("Line 5: Are Awesome\n")

print("Reading file line by line:")
for line_num, line in enumerate(read_file_generator(sample_file), 1):
    print(f"{line_num}: {line}")
print()

# Clean up
import os

os.remove(sample_file)
```

sections.title: class FloatRange, is_prime()
sections.body:
Iterator that works like range() but with float steps. Check if a number is prime.

```python
class FloatRange:
    """
    Iterator that works like range() but with float steps.
    """

    def __init__(self, start, stop, step=1.0):
        self.start = start
        self.stop = stop
        self.step = step
        self.current = start

    def __iter__(self):
        return self

    def __next__(self):
        if (self.step > 0 and self.current >= self.stop) or (
            self.step < 0 and self.current <= self.stop
        ):
            raise StopIteration

        value = self.current
        self.current += self.step
        return value

print("Float range from 0 to 2 with step 0.5:")
for num in FloatRange(0, 2, 0.5):
    print(num, end=" ")
print("\n")

print("Float range from 5 to 0 with step -0.5:")
for num in FloatRange(5, 0, -0.5):
    print(num, end=" ")
print("\n")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 11: Generator for Prime Numbers
# ============================================================================
print("=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 11: Generator for Prime Numbers")
print("=" * 70)

def is_prime(n):
    """Check if a number is prime."""
    if n < 2:
        return False
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if n % i == 0:
            return False
    return True
```

sections.title: prime_generator(), stateful_generator(), measure_time()
sections.body:
Generate prime numbers up to limit.

    Args:
        limit: Maximum number to check

    Yields:
        int: Next prime number Generator that maintains state across yields.
    Demonstrates how generators remember their state. Measure execution time of a function.

```python
def prime_generator(limit):
    """
    Generate prime numbers up to limit.

    Args:
        limit: Maximum number to check

    Yields:
        int: Next prime number
    """
    for num in range(2, limit + 1):
        if is_prime(num):
            yield num

print("Prime numbers up to 50:")
primes = list(prime_generator(50))
print(primes)
print(f"Count: {len(primes)} primes\n")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 12: Stateful Generator
# ============================================================================
print("=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 12: Stateful Generator")
print("=" * 70)

def stateful_generator():
    """
    Generator that maintains state across yields.
    Demonstrates how generators remember their state.
    """
    state = {"count": 0, "total": 0}

    while True:
        value = yield state
        if value is None:
            break
        state["count"] += 1
        state["total"] += value
        state["average"] = state["total"] / state["count"]

# Using stateful generator
gen = stateful_generator()
next(gen)  # Prime the generator

print("Adding values and tracking state:")
print(f"Add 10: {gen.send(10)}")
print(f"Add 20: {gen.send(20)}")
print(f"Add 30: {gen.send(30)}")
print(f"Add 15: {gen.send(15)}")
print()

# ============================================================================
# Performance Comparison
# ============================================================================
print("=" * 70)
print("PERFORMANCE COMPARISON")
print("=" * 70)

import time

def measure_time(func, *args):
    """Measure execution time of a function."""
    start = time.time()
    result = func(*args)
    end = time.time()
    return result, end - start
```

sections.title: list_approach(), generator_approach()
sections.body:
Create list of squares. Create generator of squares.

```python
def list_approach(n):
    """Create list of squares."""
    return [x**2 for x in range(n)]

def generator_approach(n):
    """Create generator of squares."""
    return (x**2 for x in range(n))

n = 1000000

# List approach
list_result, list_time = measure_time(list_approach, n)
print(f"List creation time: {list_time:.6f} seconds")
print(f"List size: {sys.getsizeof(list_result):,} bytes")

# Generator approach
gen_result, gen_time = measure_time(generator_approach, n)
print(f"Generator creation time: {gen_time:.6f} seconds")
print(f"Generator size: {sys.getsizeof(gen_result):,} bytes")

print(f"\nSpeed difference: {abs(list_time - gen_time):.6f} seconds")
print(f"Memory saved: {sys.getsizeof(list_result) - sys.getsizeof(gen_result):,} bytes")

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("All examples completed successfully!")
print("=" * 70)
```
